## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4498a30d3e350e1556e20c1071f69fde25d4b31c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .github/workflows/fleet-patrols.yml (`job:governed-merges-audit`) + scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs (the audit-card region: readAuditSweep, readAuditCardRows, auditRulingCandidates, auditCloseRuling, ruledAuditRows, composeAuditCard, loadAuditRulingAccounts, auditRefreshOrderFault, and the battery), scripts/check-platform-checklist-watchdog.mjs (header prose)

Read: card #33814 (body, comments 6893886312, 6896359697, 6896789431), PR #33982 (body, 3 files, net diff against `main`), the check-runs on this head. No Ruling or Maintainer-action line on the card beyond its filing shape (ruling B on #33718).

### ① Derived judgments

- Tier H by content holds: the diff rewrites a job holding `issues: write` and `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`. The PR is a draft, authored by `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay) for `os-steve`; it needs a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` approval before the owning seat lands it.
- Check-runs on this head at read time (50 runs): 23 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 11 still in progress. Green and relevant: `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Weekly governed-merges audit` (the job itself, on a real runner: clone, sweep, and the verdict step's import of the script), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Changeset`, `Platform checklist gate sweep`. ⚠️ Pending, not yet a verdict: `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test UI (1/16)`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`. This PASS is the contract review only; the landing waits on those.
- The card step never runs on a `pull_request` (its `if:` is unchanged), so `loadAuditRulingAccounts`, the `listEvents` read and the comment-then-update order have no runner evidence, only the battery and the dev's offline fake-client run. That is inherent to the step, not a defect of the PR; its first live run is on `main`.
- Refactor fidelity, read line against line with the removed inline script: every reading is kept or deliberately changed. Kept: the repo rows (UNAUDITED, WINDOW EDGE), breach rows and their keys, arm NOT MEASURED, attribution unavailable, the two exit/`complete` cross-checks, the no-JSON row and the stderr tail (last 6,000 chars, fences defused), verdict and counts, the 40/100 caps, the anchor lookup, the `Swept` cadence, the empty-card refusal, the "all ruled, nothing unread: file nothing" branch. Old cards read back the same (the carried mark keeps its prefix, the ruled heading and the footer keep their openings). Changed on purpose: N4, N8, N9, N10, N12, N13, N14/N16/N17, N15, N18.
- Data passed: the job hands the functions exactly what they read (`exit`, `raw`, `stderr`; the open card's number and body; each candidate's body, `state_reason`, `closed_at` and last `closed` event actor and `commit_id`; the run meta). `findings.json` survives the step hop as plain JSON; the `Map` stays inside one step.
- Permissions and token: unchanged (`contents: read`, `issues: write`, `pull-requests: read`; no hunk touches them). The one new API call, `issues.listEvents`, is a read inside `issues`. Importing the script from the checkout widens nothing: the sweep step already ran the PR-carried script with the token.
- Injection: no workflow expression carries untrusted text into a `run:` step or a script body. The only expression in a `run:` is the unchanged `steps.sweep.outputs.exit_code` (a shell `$?`). Subjects, reasons, slugs and actors pass `auditClean` (one line, no angle bracket, no live `@`), so a subject cannot open a heading, a fence or a second row.
- Floors: battery floor 40 against 40 assertions run (36 call sites, one in a 5-case loop); roster floor 38 to 39 with one new roster row. `batteryFloorFailures` is pushed after the last battery and before the verdict line.

Findings claimed fixed, each checked both ways against the tree:

- N4 holds: `pr == null` adds a NOT MEASURED row; the control (a PR landing on its record) stays clean.
- N5 holds: both header passages say five jobs.
- N8 holds: fitted under 60,000 chars (stderr, then NOT MEASURED, then BREACH from the tail), rows cut at 1,000; heading and comment count rows on the card. See S3.
- N9 holds: `createComment` precedes `update`, pinned off the workflow text by `auditRefreshOrderFault`; a failed comment leaves the old body, so `fresh` is recomputed next run. The mark quotes what this run read when it read the row in another state, and keeps the old wording only when the key is absent from `readings`.
- N10 holds for the cases tried, with one residual (S1). Bot close: rules nothing. Non-approver close: rules nothing. Closing keyword, even by an approver: rules nothing (`commit_id`). Stale bot: rules nothing. Unreadable or missing event, or no approver list: rules nothing. Reopen then close: the LAST `closed` event governs, so an approver's close followed by anyone else's re-close rules nothing, and a seat's close followed by an approver's reopen and close rules. Approver who is also the PR author: the close rules; no per-row author test exists, which matches the card contract (the maintainer rules, by closing).
- N12 holds: every ruling card in the horizon is read, newest card wins the mapping; a non-ruling older card still rules nothing.
- N13 holds: keyed rows outside every known section are counted and named in the comment.
- N14/N16/N17 hold as far as they go (S2 is the edge N14 opens).
- N15 holds: `AUDIT_CARD.ruledHorizonDays` is its own constant, pinned at or above 7 d + 1 h; the env comment says clone depth only; the overstated sentence is gone.
- N18 holds: the body states the day bound and who rules.

### ② Semver level

- None. No package, no published schema, no `skills/**` path. `skip-changeset` is right and `Check Changeset` is green. `Clause-②: no` is right: CI tooling and one workflow job.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` on behalf of `os-steve`; implementer session `session_01ADHkmQ9yJPqAUnGqQvBK47`, reviewer session differs. SQL push-down: n/a.
- Deviation 1 (the region did not exist, so the PR creates it): accepted. It sits between `rendering` and `CLI`, after the arm loader it reuses (`ARM_READER_SOURCE`), clear of the regions #33539, #33765 and #33846 hold. The file surface in the claim named this file's audit regions, so no breach.
- Deviation 2 and the open question (N1, N7 left open): accepted as safe for a `Part of #33814` PR. Both fail toward an extra NOT MEASURED row, never toward a hidden BREACH. The PR body ticks neither, line 1 is `Part of`, and the job header names the gap. Truthful. Answer to the question: A is the seat-level path and needs no ruling, after #33765 lands; B changes the `Maintainer-action:` contract and is the maintainer's call only if A proves insufficient; C is what the tree does until then. ⚠️ N4 widens N7's class by design (a PR-less row can never be read by a re-run); keep that under N7 on the card.
- Out-of-scope note (`stale.yml` does not exempt `governed-merges-audit`): a real gap. An open audit card is by definition unruled; after 74 idle days the stale bot closes it and its carried BREACH rows outside the window are gone. Escalated: the seat files a follow-up card (one label added to `exempt-issue-labels`, another Tier H workflow file). Not this PR's to fix.
- Card bookkeeping: #33814 stays open. Tick only what landed; add S1, S2 and S3 below as new items.

### ④ Design judgment

S1 (should-fix) — N10's "by hand" is read as "an approver's login and no commit", not as a hand. `auditCloseRuling` never reads the event's `performed_via_github_app`. `hotlong` is in `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` and is also a seat account (the triage comment 6893886312 on this card is a seat session on it), and this repo has measured user-account writes signed by the `claude` app (scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs). A seat session on an approver's account that closes the audit card therefore reads as the maintainer's ruling, and the rows it held are not announced again: the one direction that hides a BREACH. The battery's `a-seats-close` case uses the relay bot only. This is parity with the queue guard's own login test and strictly narrower than before the PR, so it does not block a `Part of` PR; but the header's and the PR body's "a seat's close rules nothing" overstate. Fix either way: pass the field through and rule nothing when an app signed the close, with a case for it, or word the claim as the login test it is.

S2 (should-fix) — the fence skip (N14) adds a silent drop. `readAuditCardRows` toggles on any line opening with three backticks or three tildes, either marker closing the other, and never reports a fence left open. A hand-pasted unclosed fence above the BREACH rows, or a quoted stderr line that starts with `~~~` (only backticks are defused), makes every later line unread: rows are not carried, and the comment still says 0 unkeyed, 0 stray, footer found. Before this PR those rows were read. Report an open fence at the end of the read the way `footer: false` is reported, and close a fence only on its own marker.

S3 (should-fix) — rows that do not fit are named by count only, and the comment's "the run log and the artifact hold them" is false for carried rows. The fit trims from the tail, where carried rows sit; a carried row outside the window is in no sweep JSON and no run summary. The wording predates this PR at the 100-row cap, but N8 lowers the point at which it applies. Name the dropped keys in the comment (they are short) and drop the claim for carried rows.

Nits:
- The `Maintainer-action:` line still says done when a manual run reads no NOT MEASURED row, which a PR-less row cannot satisfy inside the window; the row's own text says so. Belongs to N7.
- A closed card's body is read as it stands now, not as it stood at the close; an edit after an approver's close adds ruled keys. Pre-existing.
- On the create path only `prior` is explained; other closed cards that rule nothing are named only in a refresh comment.
- `approvers.includes(actor)` is case-exact; a differently cased login rules nothing (fails safe).

No must-fix. Should-fix: S1, S2, S3, carried on #33814.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bdb2a307081e2ac2741f69da03802e3a7dcbdc36`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .github/workflows/fleet-patrols.yml (`job:governed-merges-audit`) + scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs (the audit-card region: readAuditSweep, readAuditCardRows, auditRulingCandidates, auditCloseRuling, ruledAuditRows, composeAuditCard, loadAuditRulingAccounts, auditRefreshOrderFault, and the battery), scripts/check-platform-checklist-watchdog.mjs (header prose)

Delta round on record 6896878561 (head `4498a30d`). Read: the delta `4498a30d..bdb2a307` (one commit, 2 files, +67/−21), the net diff against `main`, the PR body, card #33814's comments, the check-runs on this head, and 300 live issue events of this repo (GET only) to test S1's premise.

### ① Derived judgments

- Nothing else moved. `4498a30d` is an ancestor of this head; the delta touches only the two `hits` files. In the workflow: the header sentence on who rules, the step comment, and the one `close = { … app }` line. In the script: the stderr defuse, the fence reader, `auditCloseRuling`, the dropped-row wording, and the battery. The watchdog file, the permissions, the token, the `if:` guards and the write order are as reviewed. Everything in record 6896878561 outside S1, S2 and S3 stands.
- Check-runs on this head (52 runs): 37 success, 14 skipped, 0 failed, 1 in progress. Green: `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Weekly governed-merges audit`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Platform checklist gate sweep`, `Test Core`, `Test UI`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build & E2E UI`. ⚠️ One `PR-body guards` run is still in progress (an earlier run of the same name is green).
- Floors: the battery declares 51 and runs 51 (40 before; +3 for S1, +5 for S2, +3 for S3; one existing S3-adjacent case reworded). Roster floor stays 39. The floor check still precedes the verdict line.
- Tier H, the draft state, the author (`objectstack-fleet[bot]` for `os-steve`) and the labels are unchanged.

### ② Semver level

- None. `skip-changeset` and `Clause-②: no` are right; no package or published schema is touched.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` on behalf of `os-steve`. SQL push-down: n/a.
- The deviations and the N1/N7 open question are answered in record 6896878561 and unchanged: A is the seat-level path after #33765; the PR stays `Part of #33814`.
- ⚠️ The PR body ticks `[x] S1`. This record keeps S1 open (below), so the tick is not yet true; untick it or add the measurement. On the card, S1 stays an open item; S2 and S3 close.
- The `stale.yml` follow-up card is still owed by the seat.

### ④ Design judgment

S1 (should-fix) — kept open: the code is right in shape, but its premise is unmeasured on the endpoint it reads, and what was measured contradicts it. The job reads `performed_via_github_app` off `issues.listEvents`. On 300 live events of this repo read for this round, the key is always served and always `null`, including every one of the 273 events whose actor is a `Bot` (66 of them `closed`): acts that an App signed by definition. The measurement the docstring cites (`scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`) was taken on comments and issue rows, not on events. So on the evidence at hand the events payload does not name the signing app, the new branch never fires, and a seat session closing the card on `hotlong`'s account still reads as the maintainer's hand. Whether a user-account close through the `claude` app populates the field on an event is not shown either way; the battery pins only the pure function and that the workflow text mentions the field. Meanwhile the job header now states flatly that a close signed by a GitHub App "rules nothing", a stronger claim than the one this finding first called an overstatement. Not a regression (the reading is still strictly narrower than before the PR, and at parity with the queue guard's login test), so it does not block a `Part of` PR. To close it: measure one known seat close made on a user account (the events row, and the timeline row if events stay empty), read the app from wherever it is actually served, and pin that specimen; or word the header, the docstring and the PR body as the login test it is, with the app read as best effort.

Probes on S1, for the record: an approver's reopen through an app followed by a hand close rules (the last `closed` event governs; correct). A hand close followed by an app reopen and re-close rules nothing on the same evidence as above only if the field is served. A non-string truthy `app` rules nothing and is cleaned before it is printed.

S2 — closed. A fence opens on up to three spaces and three or more of one marker; it closes only on the same character, at least as long, with nothing but whitespace after it. Tried: an opener with an info string opens and its info-string twin does not close it; a closer indented four spaces is not a closer; a block-quoted fence is no fence, so its lines are read (a quoted row counts as unkeyed, never as a row); a line opening with an inline code span is taken as an opener and, never closed, is reported. An unclosed fence with the footer present reports `openFence` with `footer: true` (the footer bound is taken before the fence pass); with the footer also gone, both warnings print. The job's own stderr quote can no longer open or close a fence (both markers defused). The cases run both ways.

S3 — closed. The comment names every dropped key, split into this run's and carried ones, and the false run-log claim for carried rows is gone from body and comment. Carried keys come only from `AUDIT_ROW_KEY` (`PR #` digits, or `commit` hex); live keys are the same `auditRowKey` values the comment already printed as "new to this card", so no new text reaches the comment. The body gains counts only, and the fit loop measures the rendered body with that line in it, so the 60,000 bound holds. The body's overflow line still opens with `… and `, which the reader skips.

Nits:
- The job collapses "field absent", "field null" and "app object with neither `slug` nor `name`" into `app: null`, which reads as a hand close. Test presence of the object, not its name, and treat an absent key as unreadable (the repo's own `artefactChannel` keeps those three apart). Fold into S1.
- A live row that did not fit is still listed under "BREACH rows new to this card" and counted in "read again", one line above the line that says it is not on the card.
- The dropped-key list is unbounded; a comment over GitHub's limit would fail, and with the comment-first order the body would then never move. Needs thousands of rows; cap the list with a count.
- The nits of record 6896878561 stand (the `Maintainer-action:` done-when against a PR-less row; a closed card's body read as it stands now; unruled cards unnamed on the create path; case-exact logins).

No must-fix. Should-fix: S1, kept open on #33814. S2 and S3 closed.
